role.altitude: The biostatistician keeps teaching sessions, grading assignments and talking with participants; building practice datasets by hand, answering the same questions by mail and helping each participant install software shrink.
skills_to_grow: Running courses on a prepared analysis environment
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose course time goes to explaining methods, not to setup.

tasks.short: Plan the course and update slides, prepare exercises with datasets and solutions, set up software access, teach graduate or continuing education courses or seminars in biostatistics, answer questions, grade assignments and talk with participants.

steps.what: Biostatistician plans the course and updates slides

loop.input: The biostatistician's outline and existing slides.
loop.check: The biostatistician reads every slide and checks every formula and example.
loop.stop: The biostatistician writes slides by hand when two drafts are wrong.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each course adds new methods and examples.

steps.what: Biostatistician builds practice datasets and solution code by hand
Biostatistician helps participants install the statistical software
Biostatistician teaches the courses or seminars in biostatistics
Biostatistician answers the same participant questions several times by mail
Biostatistician talks with participants after sessions

tasks.design: Practice datasets are simulated by script with known parameters, so each exercise has a checked answer, and the solution code runs against them, instead of datasets built by hand. Participants work in a prepared analysis environment with the packages installed, instead of each one getting install help. A course forum lets one answer reach every participant. Slide updates start from a draft that the biostatistician checks line by line. Teaching, grading and talking with participants stay with the biostatistician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Datasets were built by hand and software installed per participant.
tasks.enabler_now: Simulated teaching data, prepared analysis environments and course forums.
tasks.still_hard: Real clinical data that cannot be shared in class.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a mixed model fits when students see only formulas.

reach.learn: Whether the first session starts without install problems.

evidence.claim: Tables, figures and data simulation are deterministic code that can be checked by running it.

assumptions: Boundary: teaching courses; writing analysis code for studies (task 16249) and preparing tables and graphs of clinical data (task 16252) are sibling tasks.
Simulated datasets replace real patient data in class.
Teaching, grading and talking keep their full time.
research_questions: Is preparation time per course shorter?

incremental.description: Biostatistician maintains the analysis environment and simulation scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: repeat courses where slides and datasets barely change, so the draft and simulation scripts save little (s1 keeps 95, s2 keeps 90) (5.8); high: new courses with many exercises (10.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
